standard.title: Share arts works with audiences
standard.description: share their arts works with audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have experience sharing work informally with teachers during play or activity time, but have not yet engaged in deliberate presentation to an audience — where the relationship between maker and viewer is conscious and considered.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share arts works with an audience and engage with that audience's responses.

nodes.label: Preparing to share
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can prepare a work to share — selecting what to present and thinking about who will see or hear it.
nodes.minimum_width: Choose one arts work to share and identify the audience (teacher, small group, or class).
nodes.typical_width: Select and sequence arts work for sharing; practise presenting a performance or retelling; use digital devices to curate or document work before sharing; prepare an introduction or description of the work.
wider: Curate (select and order) a sequence of digital images to document steps in an arts process — adding commentary about what each step communicates or what was discovered
Practise a performance (song, soundscape, story retelling) using skills learnt, such as matching starting pitch or staying in time with a group

response_modes.reason: The curation and selection step is often skipped at Foundation — students benefit from deliberate practice in choosing what to present, as this builds the habit of audience awareness that underpins all future presenting work.

success_criteria: Student can identify what work they will share and who their audience is
Student has made at least one preparation choice (what to include, how to introduce it)

nodes.label: Presenting to an audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share an arts work with an audience and explain what it communicates or how it was made.
nodes.minimum_width: Share one arts work with a teacher or small group; respond to at least one question (e.g. 'What is going on in your work?') with a description connected to the work.
nodes.typical_width: Present arts works to peers in gallery, performance or digital formats; use positive language to describe own and others' works; explain themes, processes or features when asked; talk about what was enjoyed during making.
wider: Participate in a class gallery or performance walk — comment on peers' works using observational language (similarities, differences, use of materials, patterns, pathways, lines)
Present a story retelling to another class or group (through dramatic play, puppets or digital capture) — introduce the work and describe favourite moments
Present a performance of a song, soundscape or chant/rap — introduce it and explain the choices made during the creation
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot present a work and engage with an audience's response at Foundation, the feedback loop between making and audience that underlies all subsequent arts learning does not form.

response_modes.reason: Vary the presentation contexts — gallery walk, live performance, digital sharing, small group retelling — so students encounter multiple audience types and relationships, not only teacher-directed sharing.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The variety of sharing contexts at Foundation (gallery, performance, digital, retelling to another class) is rich for building audience awareness — students who share in multiple contexts develop a much stronger intuition for the maker-audience relationship.
success_criteria: Student shares their arts work with at least one other person or group
Student responds to at least one question about their work with a recognisable connection to the work's ideas or process

nodes.label: Responding to audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can engage with an audience's response to their work — listening to feedback and reflecting on what others noticed or felt.
nodes.minimum_width: Listen to at least one comment or question from an audience about their work and respond to it — either elaborating, agreeing or explaining further.
nodes.typical_width: Engage with audience responses in gallery, performance or sharing contexts; use positive language when commenting on others' work; reflect on what features of their work others noticed; describe what they enjoyed about making and sharing the work.
wider: Use digital documentation (photos or video of the sharing event) to revisit and reflect on the audience response — describing what the audience noticed and what was surprising
Participate in a gallery walk as both maker and audience member — practising both presenting and responding with constructive, observational language

response_modes.reason: Responding to audience closes the presenting cycle — connecting making, presenting and the feedback loop. Support students in treating audience response as information about communication, not just approval or disapproval.

success_criteria: Student can engage with at least one audience response (question or comment) about their work
Student can describe at least one thing the audience noticed or responded to
